clue.text: Honour a rogue

definitions.meaning: in card games the ace, king, queen and jack are the honours, and this court card is one of them
an old word for a dishonest scoundrel

explanation.surface: Someone is praising a scoundrel's honour.
explanation.definitionFit: An honour is a top court card in bridge and whist, and the jack is one; separately, the word means a villainous rascal.

clue.text: Wild West Billy-strongly recommended book

parts.note: Billy the Kid was a Wild West outlaw
in racing, a nap is a tipster's strongest tip, so napped means strongly tipped

explanation.surface: A Western outlaw's favourite novel comes highly praised.
explanation.walkthrough: A nap is a racing tipster's surest selection.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson's adventure novel is the book.

clue.text: Speak freely, party being under short notice

indicators.note: in a down entry, being under puts one piece after the other

parts.note: an advert is a notice, shortened to ad
Lib is short for the Liberal Party

explanation.surface: Talking openly at a political gathering at short notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To improvise words rather than following a script is to speak freely.

clue.text: Inspector once worked, underground

parts.note: ex means formerly, once
one who worked underground was a miner, read as was a miner

explanation.surface: An inspector who used to be a miner.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'once worked underground' as 'ex a miner', a former miner.
explanation.definitionFit: One who inspects or tests is a scrutineer or assessor.

clue.text: Does the beast carry a good deal on safari ?

definitions.text: Does the beast carry a good deal on safari ?

parts.words: Does the beast carry a good deal on safari
parts.note: the question reads as asking whether the animal shoulders a lot, describing a pack animal laden with luggage on an expedition

explanation.surface: A question about whether an animal bears much of the load on a safari.
explanation.definitionFit: A pack animal used to carry loads on journeys and expeditions is a horse that carries packs.

clue.text: And milk comes frozen home in --- (L L Lost)

definitions.text: And milk comes frozen home in --- (L L Lost)

parts.words: And milk comes frozen home in
parts.note: a line from the winter song at the close of Love's Labour's Lost, missing its final word, a bucket

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare's winter song with a word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: The milk in the song is carried home in a bucket.

clue.text: A short distance from the enemy in the middle

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: the centre is the middle
time is often called the enemy, as in the saying time is the enemy

explanation.surface: Being only a short way from hostile forces in the centre of battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The enemy' means TIME, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundredth of a metre is a tiny length.

clue.text: At the end of March going out to get gravel

indicators.note: take just the closing letter of the next word
out here means the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: In late March someone goes out to buy gravel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges GOING into OGGIN after H, March's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mix of gravel and sand used for paths, a type of surfacing.

clue.text: A caravan or the place where it rested?

definitions.text: A caravan or the place where it rested?

parts.words: A caravan or the place where it rested
parts.note: a caravan is a house on the road; also an inn by the highway where travellers stop

explanation.surface: Asking about a travelling caravan and its stopping place.
explanation.definitionFit: A wayside inn where travellers rest; and a mobile home is literally a dwelling on a highway.

clue.text: Relaxed as in a river retreat

indicators.note: one piece goes within the other
retreat means go back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: Unwinding at a riverside getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' turns DEE round to EED; AS goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To have loosened or slackened something is to have relaxed it.

clue.text: Spotted one in one hundred and one on film

definitions.text: Spotted one in one hundred and one on film

parts.words: Spotted one in one hundred and one on film
parts.note: the spotted dog breed made famous by the Disney film about a hundred and one puppies

explanation.surface: Someone picks out a single dog from the hundred and one in a famous movie.
explanation.definitionFit: The film 101 Dalmatians concerns a hundred and one of these spotted dogs, so any one of them fits.

clue.text: Grand wench in see-through material

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds
an old word for a young woman, a lass

explanation.surface: A young woman wearing a transparent garment.
explanation.definitionFit: The transparent substance used in windows is the commonest see-through material.

clue.text: Table one is out though

indicators.note: letters that are out of place are put back in a new arrangement

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: A table is missing, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is out' signals rearranging TABLE plus I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: A conjunction meaning even though or although.

clue.text: Polished all over

definitions.meaning: given a final smooth surface or refined, as a well-made piece is

explanation.surface: Something gleams after being rubbed everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A polished product has a fine surface treatment; and something all over is completed and ended.

clue.text: Tolerate nevertheless a period of inactivity

parts.note: to stand something is to tolerate it
still can mean nevertheless, as in still, it was worth it

explanation.surface: Putting up with a lull anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: A halt in which nothing moves is a time with no activity.

clue.text: Shops perhaps for correct neckwear

parts.note: proper means correct, as in the proper way
ties are worn around the neck

explanation.surface: A request for the right kind of neckties.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops are examples of real estate or buildings someone may own.

clue.text: Commissioner has order to shoot snowman but not now

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
a bud is a young shoot on a plant

indicators.note: but not tells us to take some letters out of the word before

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An official orders the shooting of a snowman, but not just yet.
explanation.walkthrough: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: An official appointed to investigate complaints against public bodies is a commissioner.

clue.text: Some doubt about part of the brass ?

indicators.note: about here signals that the phrase is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: a 'but' is an objection or doubt, so some doubt is a but

explanation.surface: Uncertainty over a section of the brass band.
explanation.walkthrough: A BUT (as in 'no ifs or buts') read backwards gives the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The large low-pitched instrument belongs to the brass section of an orchestra.

clue.text: Occult study as to Troy taking in a wooden object

indicators.note: one word takes another inside it

parts.note: taken as written
a log is a piece of wood

explanation.surface: Something about Troy and the wooden horse taken inside its walls.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the Trojan Horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading the stars to predict fortunes is an esoteric discipline.

clue.text: How one of Joshua's followers decided matters

definitions.text: How one of Joshua's followers decided matters

parts.words: How one of Joshua's followers decided matters
parts.note: the Book of Judges follows Joshua in the Bible, so one of those judges would have judged matters

explanation.surface: A biblical leader's successor reaches a ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: To have pronounced a judicial ruling is to have decided a case.

clue.text: Pecks of fishes

definitions.meaning: light touches or pats, as a bird gives with its beak
small flatfish found in British waters

explanation.surface: A bird pecking at some fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Light pats or touches are small strikes; and the word also names a family of small flatfish.

clue.text: Eye of newt, toe of frog-or engine dirt possibly.

definitions.text: Eye of newt, toe of frog

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A list of witches' potion items, or perhaps grime from a motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eye of newt and toe of frog' is from the witches' brew in Macbeth; 'possibly' rearranges ENGINE DIRT.
explanation.definitionFit: Each item in the witches' recipe in Macbeth is one component of the brew.

clue.text: In the manner of a spirit warning

parts.note: the French phrase a la means in the manner of
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Like a ghostly warning.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic term for a call to arms or alarm signal.

clue.text: Like weak wine or the Cheshire Cat's grin

definitions.meaning: thin wine is said to lack body
in Alice in Wonderland the cat vanishes leaving its grin hanging without any torso

explanation.surface: Comparing feeble wine with a disappearing feline smile.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine without body is thin; the Cheshire Cat's grin floated in the air without a torso attached.

clue.text: Encouragement of vulgarity down under

definitions.meaning: read as two words, an urging to be base or coarse

explanation.surface: Promoting crudeness in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Split into two words it urges someone to be coarse; as one word it means beneath.

clue.text: Plug another hole to contain the water

indicators.note: the run of words holds the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Fixing a further leak to stop water escaping.
explanation.walkthrough: The water is a Swiss-Italian lake, hidden in 'pLUG ANOther'; 'the water' tempts as the stuff being plugged.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Lugano is a body of water on the Swiss-Italian border.

clue.text: Excuse for one to get bail perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters could be rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A pretext for someone to be granted bail.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim that one was elsewhere at the time, used as a defence.

clue.text: The ones in hand

parts.note: in a card game, the cards ranking as one held in one's hand

explanation.surface: Things currently held.
explanation.definitionFit: Cards with a single pip, held in a card player's hand.

clue.text: Night-climber catches bird in both hands

indicators.note: one piece holds the other as if catching it

parts.note: L and R, left and right hands
the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: A nocturnal climber seizes a bird with two hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturnal tree-dwelling primate of Madagascar that climbs at night.

clue.text: Henry V as Harry le Roy, :for instance

definitions.text: Henry V as Harry le Roy, :for instance

parts.words: Henry V as Harry le Roy
parts.note: in Shakespeare's Henry V the king walks his camp in disguise and calls himself Harry le Roy to a soldier

explanation.surface: Describing the king's alias in Shakespeare's history play.
explanation.definitionFit: A king going among his troops under a false name is in disguise, hiding his identity.

clue.text: Breezy workers of the countryside

parts.note: rural machines powered by the wind that grind corn

explanation.surface: Cheerful farm labourers.
explanation.definitionFit: Wind-driven mills in rural areas grind grain, working by breeze.

clue.text: Paper cleaner

definitions.meaning: a British term for a domestic help who comes in each day

explanation.surface: A newspaper and a household helper.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper issued each weekday; and in Britain a char who cleans homes.
